messages:
Maya: Heads-up — after the 11:30 release we're seeing a noticeable perf regression on gen endpoints in us-west1 (A10 pools). p95 token latency jumped ~45% and throughput dropped ~18%. Canary flagged this morning.
Sam: Any upstream CI perf failures or regressions?
Maya: CI perf job did fail on the nightly run but it was noisy and got a flaky label; we missed the alert. CI-Bot posted a perf-check failure at 1710589000: `p95 > baseline + 20%` for gen-workload-smallseq.
Liam: Do you have concrete numbers / profiling output?
Maya: Quick paste from profiling: 
```
endpoint: gen-v2
region: us-west1-a
hardware: A10G
baseline p95: 120ms (tokens/sec: 240)
current p95: 175ms (tokens/sec: 198)
avg batch_size: 2.1 -> 3.8
kv cache hit-rate: 86% -> 61%
kernel selected: cuBLAS_fastpath -> fallback_kernel_v2
```
Maya: Notable: kernel selection moved to `fallback_kernel_v2` for many requests. We also see KV cache miss rate spike — looks correlated with a recent change to shard routing (PR: `rwd-infer/dispatch#487`).
Anya: Which commits landed in the release?
Maya: Release includes: `aa9f3d7` (batching heuristics tweak), `bb2c1a0` (kernel selection refactor), `cc3d442` (KV shard rebalance).
Liam: I ran a git bisect against the canary image on a repro harness in staging. Bisect indicates `bb2c1a0` is the first that reproduces the latency regression on A10. On H100 the regression is much smaller (~5-7%).
Sam: That suggests kernel selection change picks a suboptimal kernel on A10 for our typical seq length distribution. Any kernel selection logs?
Maya: Yes, attached snippet from runtime log: `kernel_selector: score_fastpath=0.23 score_fallback=0.78 chosen=fallback_kernel_v2 reason=heuristic_threshold`
Anya: Can we force a kernel override in the canary (env var `RW_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fastpath`) to confirm?
Maya: Did that — performance returns to baseline on A10. p95 back to ~125ms. So override proves kernel choice is the culprit.
Liam: Why does fallback_kernel_v2 get a higher heuristic score on A10? It should prefer the fastpath (cuBLAS) unless memory/kv/cache footprint forces fallback. Maybe the change in batching heuristics (`aa9f3d7`) increased observed batch sizes => different kernel scoring.
Maya: Exactly — batch_timeout bumped from 12ms -> 25ms in `aa9f3d7`, so we end up with larger batches for low-TPS services. Larger batches increase peak memory, which seems to push kernel selector toward fallback on A10. H100 has enough memory and different kernel perf envelope so impact is small.
Sam: That explains hardware-specific difference (A10 vs H100). How about L4?
Liam: L4 shows moderate regression (~20% p95) — its kernel perf curves lie between A10 & H100.
CI-Bot: perf-ci: nightly perf job 1710589000: gen-workload-smallseq failed threshold. Regression suspected in `bb2c1a0` and `aa9f3d7`.
Ops-Bot: Ops notes: around same window on eu-central-2 we also saw increased network egress spikes; not sure if related but noisy neighbor reports on A10 cluster at 11:40 (host 10.12.5.22).
Maya: I dug into KV cache behavior — KV eviction rate increased after `cc3d442` because shard mapping changes caused cache keys to miss until warmed. That amplifies load and memory pressure. So three interacting changes: batching up, kernel refactor, KV rebalance. Combo pushes A10 into fallback kernel.
Anya: Proposed mitigations: 1) immediate revert of `bb2c1a0` kernel selection refactor (hotfix), 2) reduce `batch_timeout` back to 12ms for gen endpoints, 3) delay/kick off KV rebalance with a rolling warm-up. Which do we prefer for fastest rollback?
Sam: Revert `bb2c1a0` is smallest blast radius and immediately fixes kernel choice per Maya's override test. Also create a follow-up to tune `batch_timeout`.
Liam: I'll open the revert PR now and add a CI perf gate that runs a quick A10 microbenchmark in presubmit. If CI fails again we'll block merges.
Maya: Revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/512 (opened). Rolling canary paused.
CI-Bot: perf-ci: triggered quick-smoke A10 microbenchmark — running...
Anya: For rollout blockers: mark the release paused in Console, and notify SRE to check noisy neighbor hosts in us-west1 A10 pool.
Ops-Bot: SRE alerted. We're isolating the noisy host 10.12.5.22 and throttling its workload.
Sam: Next steps timeline: - revert PR merge + canary -> confirm p95 back to baseline (30–60m) - if good, resume rollout with `batch_timeout` change held for follow-up - KV rebalance postponed and reworked with warm-up plan.
Maya: Notes for postmortem: interaction of batching heuristic & kernel selector + KV rebalance caused non-linear perf regression on smaller-memory GPUs (A10). Add targeted perf tests per hardware type (A10/L4/H100) to CI matrix.
Liam: Also adding a kernel selection unit test to prevent heuristics regression and a perf threshold on presubmit for the gen endpoint on representative hardware emulation.
Sam: Thanks everyone. If the revert doesn't land in 30m we escalate. :thumbsup:
Maya: Will update thread with canary stats after revert.
CI-Bot: perf-ci: revert merged at 1710601500 by Liam. Quick canary run scheduled.
Maya: Canary after revert: p95=128ms, throughput recovered, kv hit-rate slowly warming. Rolling canary resumed.
Anya: Marking this as resolved for the release blocker; will file a follow-up to track KV rebalance plan and batch heuristic tuning. :white_check_mark:
